correctness.rationale: For any two class sums the product coefficient at cell (i,j) is the left class's row count at i times the right class's column count at j. Equality within each target class for every pair of factors implies equality of each complete profile, by separately summing over the factors and cancelling 2 or m in characteristic zero. Conversely equal profiles suffice. Unequal row profiles force all classes into single rows; any two columns sharing one class must share the corresponding class in the other row, giving a common column partition. If all classes are row-balanced, a class name fixes the unordered pair of class names on any column it meets, and a two-name component is balanced exactly when each orientation occurs on half its columns. These descriptions are unique. Row and column classes are intrinsic as principal right and left ideals, so the automorphisms are precisely the independent row and column permutations. For balanced components a single row swap combined with matching half-swaps, together with independent column permutations within the prescribed pieces, gives exactly the prescribed orbits. The labelled assembly weight is 1 plus half the central binomial coefficient on even components, and 1 on odd components, giving the stated EGF with the formal constant 2.
correctness.reproduction: Run python3 /workspace/branches/04593389-5367-42c3-bc38-efa3a29b9983/independent_check.py. The independent checker exhausts labelled partitions at m=1..4, tests product coefficients, compares accepted partitions with the classification and their orbits, and evaluates the weighted recurrence to m=9. Separated/balanced counts are 1/1, 2/3, 5/8, 15/33 at m=1..4; the recurrence gives the nine stated totals.
residual_risks: Exhaustive direct testing ends at m=4; weighted recurrence evaluations are not exhaustive partition counts. The proof is restricted to the stated characteristic-zero setting.
